dedupe_keys.name: nyc dot bicycle and pedestrian counts automated count sensors

description: New York City's Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) publishes counts of cyclists and pedestrians from automated sensors at key locations on NYC Open Data. Coverage: New York City count sites; the counts table gives the sensor, travel mode, direction, flow identifier and name, timestamp, granularity, count and a status flag, and a companion sensors table lists each site's position, first and last data dates, granularity, travel modes, whether counts are directional and timestamped, and counter installation dates. Since 28 January 2026 these two tables replace the older Bicycle Counters dataset, which is kept as historical data. The counts are refreshed daily, the data change every 15 minutes, and times are in Eastern time. Format and access: Socrata tables with CSV export and an API. Licence and cost: free under the NYC Open Data terms; no separate licence is named. Caveats: DOT warns of gaps caused by weather, connection interruptions, equipment faults and vandalism, and makes no claim about accuracy. The counts can be used to calibrate cycling and walking flows in network flow models of New York and to measure changes after street redesigns or disruptions. It relates to Citi Bike system data and the Mobility Data Specification in the catalogue.
